name: Stuðlagil canyon from Klaustursel
why: Walk down the Jökla past Stuðlafoss to the floor of the basalt column canyon, the only side where you stand among the columns by the turquoise river.
book: Free; parking 1,000 ISK (Parka app). Road 923 from the Ring Road, 14 km to Klaustursel. A high-clearance car can go 2 km further to the upper car park and halve the walk.
dangers: Ropes and steep steps down into the canyon; wet rock at the bottom.
Never swim: the glacier river is near 0 °C with a strong current.
turnaround: In spring or after rain, if water covers the canyon floor, stay on the rim.

points.name: Klaustursel bridge car park
points.note: Leave the car by the bridge over the Jökla at Klaustursel farm and cross to the east bank.

points.name: Stuðlafoss
points.note: Halfway: a small fall over a ring of basalt columns, just off the track by the upper car park.

points.name: Stuðlagil canyon floor
points.note: Down the ropes to the river: hexagonal columns rise straight from the turquoise water on both sides.
